description.t:
This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

description.raw:
This course introduces students to the vital role of computers and computer programmers in shaping modern society. It
aims to foster a strong foundation in logical formulation techniques essential for programming, while promoting the
development of good coding practices. Students will be taught the fundamentals of Java programming and explore
significant real-world applications. 
In line with La Consolacion University Philippines' commitment to forming   Christo-centric Catholic professionals , the
course integrates   Marian Augustinian values   in each lesson, ensuring that students not only achieve intellectual growth
but also cultivate moral and ethical responsibility in the digital age. This holistic approach nurtures individuals who contribute
positively to society, embodying   community, humility, and love of service , as exemplified by the Blessed Virgin Mary
and Saint Augustine. By the end of the course, students will have created their own Java applications, demonstrating both
technical proficiency and a sense of purpose rooted in their Catholic faith.

description.t:
This course introduces students to the principles and practices of systems engineering, focusing on the analysis,
design, and management of complex systems. Through a blend of theoretical concepts and practical applications, students
learn   how   to   approach   and   solve   large-scale   engineering   problems   involving   multiple   components,   stakeholders,   and
operational constraints. Key topics include requirements analysis, systems design, integration, project management, and
performance evaluation. 
Students will develop skills in modeling and optimizing systems that integrate people, processes, and technology. They
will explore methods for ensuring that systems are efficient, reliable, and adaptable across various industries, such as
manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics. This course prepares BSIE students to play a vital role in creating systems that
maximize performance, minimize waste, and support organizational goals. 
Beyond   technical   knowledge,   the   course   integrates   Marian   Augustinian   values   into   each   lesson,   fostering   the
development of students as Christo-centric Catholic professionals. The curriculum not only aims for intellectual growth but also
instills a commitment to ethical decision-making, social responsibility, and compassionate service. Students will be equipped
with the knowledge and values necessary to thrive as professionals in the field of Industrial Engineering.

description.t:
This course covers operational amplifiers, signal converters, power switching devices and the construction and operation
of sensors and transducers for converting physical parameters into electrical signals and vice-versa. The course focuses
on the application of these devices in developing signal conversion circuits that allows measurement, processing and control
of physical parameters by digital processing systems such as a finite state machine or a digital computer. Topics on
actuators are also included. 
Anchored in the Marian and Augustinian values of truth (veritas), unity (unitas), and charity (caritas), the course encourages
students to design technology that promotes social responsibility, collaboration, and compassion. Through hands-on
projects, learners will not only develop technical proficiency but also embody ethical stewardship — using their knowledge to
create solutions that serve the needs of others and contribute to the common good.
